name: GeologicAI: AI core scanning and logging for mining
title: GeologicAI: AI core scanning and logging for mining
answer: GeologicAI publishes product and platform material on its AI-assisted drill core scanning and logging systems, including the Digital Core Table. The most useful single point is that its Auto Lithology algorithm is a supervised machine learning tool trained to site-specific lithological logging schemas, identifying rock units and boundaries from combined spectral and geochemical data, which shows how geology is being turned into a machine-readable input at the core tray.

sections.body: This is the website of GeologicAI, a mining technology vendor, read across 60 pages on 3 October 2026. It is a mix of product pages for core scanning, logging and data products, a blog interview with chief executive Grant Sanden conducted by Dr Tamer Elbokl of the Canadian Mining Journal, and legal pages covering website and platform terms of use. The product and blog pages carry the substantive content about artificial intelligence. The legal pages are dated, with the Platform Terms of Use last updated 3 October 2026, and they govern use of the Digital Core Table, the RMSP software, the AMP and DHO tools and the RMSP portal.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The company's core proposition is that drill core can be scanned with multiple sensors and the resulting data processed by AI algorithms to produce high-resolution geological insight in near real time, with the interview claiming turnaround times can fall from weeks to hours. The scanning combines RGB imagery, XRF, hyperspectral and LiDAR, and the data products layer machine learning on top. Auto Lithology is described as a proprietary supervised algorithm that follows site-specific lithological logging schemas and identifies units and boundaries from integrated spectral and geochemical data. A Low Element Predictor predicts grade intervals for elements a single sensor such as XRF cannot reliably detect, by integrating multiple data sources. A site-specific supervised tool delivers matrix-specific calibration for XRF concentration outputs at one centimetre or downscaled to any user-defined interval. Hyperspectral data is unmixed at pixel level to map minerals and spectral intensity across the core surface. A convolutional neural network, trained on an image set curated by geologists from multisensory scan data, identifies sulfide minerals and maps their distribution, area percentage and grain size. Auto Sampler combines scanning data, geological logging and advanced products to generate optimised sampling intervals and QAQC samples under site-specific rules, reducing human bias. Logging pages add that AI algorithms trained on site-specific data can predict non-visible elements such as gold to flag new mineralisation zones, and that mineralisation data on bleb size, depths and interval area can be classified and exported. The company also acquired Lumo Analytics, whose LIBS-based core analysis lets its Resource Knowledge Systems detect rare-earth and light elements.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The interview states turnaround times can be reduced from weeks to hours. XRF calibration outputs are available at one centimetre or downscaled to any user-defined interval. The Platform Terms define Aggregated Data as anonymised and aggregated statistical or analytical data not identifiable to a customer, and Client Data as core, rock, drillhole, assay, geological, subsurface and imagery data, excluding Usage Data, Aggregated Data and GeologicAI Technology. The website terms state that case studies, client examples, performance figures and metrics such as processing times, logging speeds and rates of discovery are illustrative only, and that nothing on the sites is geological, engineering, technical, legal, financial or investment advice.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader tracking AI in mining, this source is a concrete account of how one specialist vendor turns geology into a machine-readable input. It names the model types in production use, supervised lithology classification, grade prediction for elements sensors miss, convolutional networks for sulfide identification, and pixel-level hyperspectral unmixing, and it ties them to physical hardware and to downstream sampling decisions. It also shows the commercial framing, faster data for project economics and risk, and the acquisition of LIBS capability for critical minerals, which is useful context for anyone assessing where computer vision in exploration is heading.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Mining

sections.body: The material is vendor published and promotional in intent, with no independent validation of accuracy or performance. The website terms explicitly describe case studies, client examples and performance figures as illustrative only, and results as dependent on deposit, data and circumstances. The blog content is an interview rather than a study, and the legal pages are contractual rather than technical. There is no detail on model error rates, training data volumes or comparative benchmarks, and the site does not cover competing approaches beyond its own products and integrations.
